descriptions.default: A low pedestal stands under the scarab.
A chapter about not letting the heart of the man act against him in the Netherworld.
The deceased kneels before the scarab with both hands raised in adoration.
A large scarab beetle with a sun disc over its head stands on a pedestal.
A low block carries the seated god.
A chapter about not depriving the man of his heart in the Netherworld.
The deceased stands with both hands raised in adoration before the god.
A tall ankh stands upright, a tied band hanging from its arms.
A god in a long wig and a striped garment sits on a pedestal with his knees drawn up, a staff beside him.
A chapter about not letting the man be deprived of his heart in the Netherworld.
The deceased kneels with the sign of the heart held against his breast and one hand raised before the four gods.

Four gods sit in a row on a bench, each wrapped in bands and holding an ankh: the first has a bird's head, the second a jackal's, the third a beast's and the fourth a man's. Davis names them Amset, Hapi, Tiaoumautef and Kebhsennouf.
A long low bench carries the four gods.
A low pedestal carries the bird.
A chapter about giving back to the man his heart in the Netherworld.
The deceased kneels with the sign of the heart held against his breast and one hand raised before the bird.
A bird with a man's head and a long wig stands on a pedestal, its tail trailing behind it: the emblem of the soul.
A chapter about making the man remember in the Netherworld.
A man stands with one hand raised in front of him.
A man stands facing him, holding a small object in one hand.
A chapter about the bringing of the magic charms by the man, with himself, in the Netherworld.
A man stands with one hand held out in front of him.
A man in a long wig stands with a tall staff in one hand.
A chapter about opening the man's mouth in the Netherworld.
A man holds a small round jar in one hand and raises the other.
A man in a long wig stands with a tall staff in his hand.

descriptions.default: A man holds out a small object on one outstretched arm and a shallow bowl in the other hand. Davis has a priest presenting a vase and the ram-headed wand to two personages.
A man stands with a long staff in one hand: the standing one of the two personages.
A man sits on a chair with a latticed side, a staff in his hand: the seated one of the two personages.
